pages.title: CA Client Integration (Online and Offline)
pages.purpose: Explain utils/cautils: the CaClient interface, online client construction against step-ca, the embedded OfflineCA authority, admin clients, bootstrap/health, and provisioner discovery.
instructions: Describe admin client construction with admin-cert/admin-key x5c flows.
Document NewClient's offline-vs-online branch, ca-url parsing (https-only, IPv6 bracket repair in flags.parseCaURL), and root fallback to the STEPPATH root CA file.
Explain OfflineCA as a singleton wrapping smallstep/certificates authority with ca.json config and password-file handling, and why the singleton exists (badgerDB lock note).
smallstep/certificates is external: characterize roles at the import boundary only.

pages.title: CLI Runtime and Command Registration
pages.purpose: Explain the process entrypoint, how the urfave/cli app is assembled, the command registration/import mechanism, plugin dispatch, middleware injection, and error/exit handling.
instructions: Document error rendering (messenger errors, STEPDEBUG), panic handler exit codes, and InjectContext middleware pattern.
Explain command.Register/Retrieve registration via blank imports and the plugin fallback (step-<name>-plugin lookup, Windows extension handling, known plugin URLs).
Trace main() -> cmd.SetName -> cmd.Run() -> step.Init() -> newApp -> app.Run(os.Args).
cli-utils (command, step, ui, usage, errs) is an external dependency: describe the contract as used from this repo, not its internals.

pages.title: Step Environment, Contexts, and Configuration
pages.purpose: Explain the on-disk step environment: STEPPATH/base path, per-context authority directories, contexts.json/current-context.json, defaults, the --config global flag, and context-related flags.
instructions: Be explicit that file layout mechanics live in the external cli-utils step package; ground claims in this repo's usage.
Document contexts.json layout, select/current/list/remove subcommands, --context/--profile/--authority and --no-context flags.
Show how flags.CaConfig defaults to $(step path)/config/ca.json and where root CA path comes from.

Use step path documentation and --base/--profile behavior to explain default $HOME/.step, STEPPATH override, and per-context authority path selection with evidence from command/path and command/context docs and code.

pages.title: Tokens, Claims, and Provisioner Authentication
pages.purpose: Explain the token package (JWT claims, options, validity limits, claim names), token/provision OTT, the token flow used by ca/ssh commands, audience paths per token type, and the x5c/sshpop/nebula/key attestation header flags.
instructions: Cover how provisioner JWTs are generated/encrypted (token_generator.go) and renew token special case.
Document default issuer/audience, MinValidity/MaxValidity bounds, and claim keys (sha, sans, step, user, cnf).
Explain parseAudience mapping of token types to /1.0/* CA endpoints and provisioner discovery via pki.GetProvisioners, plus ACME/SCEP token-flow rejection errors.
Note provisioner-key AES encryption details as delegated to go.step.sm/crypto where applicable.

pages.title: CA Administration, ACME, and OAuth
pages.purpose: Explain the ca command group surface: ca init (offline PKI bootstrap), provisioner/admin CRUD via the CA management API, ACME subcommands and acmeutils flow, ca token, plus the hidden api group and the step oauth command.
instructions: Describe ca init delegation to smallstep/certificates pki vs the CLI's own orchestration (what evidence exists here; state uncertainty about external internals).
Document ACME flow in acmeutils: account/key handling, challenge types actually referenced in this repo (e.g. http-01, dns-01, tls-alpn if present) and EAB flags.
Explain admin/provisioner commands requiring admin credentials (admin-cert/admin-key) against the management API.
Summarize oauth flows supported by command/oauth (authorization code, OOB, JWT bearer, refresh) from its registered flags/usage text.

pages.title: SSH Certificates and Agent Integration
pages.purpose: Explain the ssh command group (login, certificate, list, revoke, renew, rekey, proxycommand, config, hosts, checkHost) and internal/sshutil agent protocol client used to talk to ssh-agent over unix/pipe transports.
instructions: Document SSH_AUTH_SOCK handling and the Windows named-pipe configuration in sshutil/pipe.go.
Explain proxycommand usage pattern with ssh_config and renewal helpers; mention systemd renewer units as the operational counterpart (cross-reference build page).
Trace how step ssh obtains host/user certs through cautils flows and stores them in the SSH agent via sshutil.

pages.title: X.509 Certificate and Crypto Command Groups
pages.purpose: Explain the certificate and crypto command groups: offline X.509 create/key/csr, inspect/lint/bundle/verify/install, format/p12, and the JOSE toolkit (jwt/jws/jwe/jwk), kdf, otp, nacl, hash, rand.
instructions: Document key-generation option flow (kty/curve/size validation in utils.GetKeyDetailsFromCLI) and trust-store installation via smallstep/truststore.
Explain internal/kdf providers (scrypt/argon2/bcrypt via pkg/bcrypt_pbkdf) and cryptoutil roles.
Map subcommand structure from group registrations; do not narrate every file.
Note where implementations delegate to go.step.sm/crypto and zcrypto/zlint.

pages.title: Change Guides
pages.purpose: Focused, verification-grounded guides for representative maintenance tasks: adding a command, adding/reusing a flag, changing CA client or token behavior, extending plugin lookup, adding an integration testscript, and bumping release packaging.
instructions: Derive every step from existing code patterns, not hypotheticals; where the repo is silent (e.g. review policy), say so.

Each guide must state the files to touch, the invariants to preserve (registration import in internal/cmd/root.go, CHANGELOG requirement from docs/local-development.md), and the narrowest validation command.
Keep guidance verifiable offline: make build, make test, targeted go test paths.

pages.title: Build, Packaging, and Release Operations
pages.purpose: Explain how step is built, versioned, packaged, signed, and released: Makefile targets and version injection, GoReleaser config, Docker images, deb/rpm packages, systemd renewer units, shell completions, PowerShell installers, and GitHub workflows.
instructions: Describe systemd cert-renewer timer/service pattern and the S3 redirect note in systemd/README.md.
Do NOT cite or describe OpenWiki-owned files listed in .openwikiignore (AGENTS.md, .github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml).
Document VERSION derivation (git describe, GITHUB_REF, .VERSION fallback), LDFLAGS injection into main.Version/BuildTime, and CGO_ENABLED=0 default.
Map goreleaser build ids, archives, nfpms, signing, and checksums; note GoReleaser Pro vs OSS skip logic in the Makefile.

pages.title: Testing Strategy
pages.purpose: Explain how this repository tests itself: unit tests colocated with packages, the testscript-based integration suite that runs the real step entrypoint, testdata txtar conventions, and how to run and extend tests.
instructions: Cite real assertions; do not speculate about CI-hosted behavior beyond workflow files.
Document testscript.Main wiring: the step command is the in-process cmd.Run entrypoint, giving end-to-end coverage without spawning binaries.
Note make test uses gotestsum with -short and coverage; make race exists.
Show how txtar scripts and testdata fixtures are organized per area (testdata/certificate, testdata/crypto, testdata/help).

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Get an engineer from clone to a working, tested local build of step and oriented to the repository's major systems and where to change things.
instructions: Cover bootstrap/build/test/install loop with exact make targets and cite Makefile lines.
Map the top-level directories to their roles (cmd, command, internal, flags, token, utils, exec, integration, packaging dirs) briefly.
Point to the change guides and architecture pages rather than duplicating them.
